battle.name: 第二次塞米諾爾戰爭
battle.theater: 佛羅里達中部沼澤地帶
battle.brief: 一八三五年十二月，聯邦以《印第安人遷移法》推進塞米諾爾人遷往密西西比河以西，戴德少校率百餘人出發後在威托拉庫奇河上游遭伏擊，縱隊僅三人生還，戰爭自此全面展開。此後六年聯邦遠征軍在沼澤與棕櫚叢中追擊游散戰士，卡面長槍卻早已退出生產序列，只餘民兵操典與儀仗中的殘影。

kit.name: 長槍
kit.history: 方陣的長矛讓火槍隊站在後面。密西西比之後，長矛和火槍一起站住了。

countries: 這場戰爭的交戰雙方，一方是美國聯邦政府，實際由華盛頓的陸軍部與海軍部分頭指揮：駐紮佛羅里達的聯邦步兵師（第一、二、三、四、六、七、八師）、第二龍騎兵師、第三砲兵第九連等常備部隊，海軍陸戰隊步兵旅，海軍與緝私隊的八艘巡邏快船，以及佛羅里達、阿拉巴馬、喬治亞、南卡羅來納、密蘇里、賓夕法尼亞等州與准州民兵和自組志願兵。聯邦方面靠一套書面授權運作：安德魯·傑克遜一八三五年三月致塞米諾爾首領的公開信是最後通牒，佛羅里達總督理查德·考爾管治民營，佛羅里達印第安事務官威利·湯普森在福特金堡執行遷移令，各路部隊則依賴通訊緩慢的軍令逐次投入，屢屢出現帥令未到而戰機已失的窘境。另一方是塞米諾爾聯盟，並非單一民族，而是包括馬斯科吉（克里克）下城、科瓦塔、阿拉楚阿等支系，希奇蒂語系的米卡蘇基、尤奇等部族，數百名黑人塞米諾爾，以及被稱為「西班牙印第安人」、實為卡盧薩後裔的漁場群體。塞米諾爾方面的決策靠首領會議與村落組織：遷移與否由首領商議，作戰時推舉戰時首領率領數十人的突擊隊，婦孺隨隊遷徙並在營地中擔任後勤與戰鬥角色，糧食被毀即整村退回沼澤。實力對比懸殊：聯邦可湊出常備軍、民兵、志願兵與海軍合計逾萬人，塞米諾爾開戰時只有九百至一千四百名戰士，傷亡無從補充。
countriesEn: The two belligerents of this war were, on the one side, the United States federal government, which directed the war through the War Department and the Navy Department in Washington: the federal infantry regiments in Florida (the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 6th, 7th and 8th), ten companies of the 2nd Dragoons, nine companies of the 3rd Artillery, a brigade of Marine infantry, the Navy and eight revenue cutters, together with militia and self-organized volunteers from Florida, Alabama, Georgia, South Carolina, Missouri and Pennsylvania. The federal side ran on written authority: President Andrew Jackson's open letter to the Seminole chiefs in March 1835 was the ultimatum, Florida territorial governor Richard K. Call oversaw the volunteers, and Florida Indian agent Wiley Thompson enforced the removal order at Fort King, while the field columns were fed by slow-moving dispatches, a situation that repeatedly produced the reverse of the intended effect, orders arriving after the moment to act had already passed. On the other side stood a Seminole confederation that was not a single people but a bundle of peoples: the Muscogee (Creek) Lower Towns, Coweta and Alachua bands; the Hitchiti-speaking Mikasuki and Uchee groups; several hundred Black Seminoles; and the so-called 'Spanish Indians' of the coastal fishing ranchos, who were in fact descendants of the Calusa. Decision-making on the Seminole side rested on chiefs' councils and village organization: migration was debated and decided in council, and in war each war chief led a war party of a few dozen men. Women and children moved with the columns, handling logistics and fighting in the camp, and when stores were destroyed the whole village withdrew into the swamp. The imbalance in strength was extreme: the federals could raise more than ten thousand men from regulars, militia, volunteers and the Navy, while the Seminoles began the war with between nine hundred and fourteen hundred warriors and had no means of replacing their losses.
people: 聯邦一方的關鍵人物，開戰前是總統安德魯·傑克遜與印第安事務局：傑克遜的遷移信件，以及陸軍上校鄧肯·克林奇不斷報稱塞米諾爾無意遷徙，才迫使華盛頓把地方官員的交涉升級為軍事行動；佛羅里達印第安事務官威利·湯普森禁止售槍售藥、褫奪不願遷移首領的權位，最終在一八三五年十月末與塞米諾爾交火時身亡。作戰序列上接連走馬換將：埃德蒙·蓋恩斯、溫菲爾德·斯科特先後主持戰局，湯瑪斯·傑薩普於一八三六年十二月接任，一八三八年五月由扎卡里·泰勒接掌，一八四一年五月再由沃克·基思·阿米斯蒂德與威廉·詹金斯·沃思接手；戴德少校率兩個連離開福特布魯克，踏上威托拉庫奇河方向的山路，其子喬治·阿米斯蒂德隨隊陣亡。生還者蘭塞姆·克拉克於一八三九年出版《佛羅里達印第安人奇遇記》，是聯邦方面唯一的當事記述；伊桑·艾倫·希區克的行軍日誌留下最尖銳的批評，指責政府違約逼人起戰。威廉·特庫姆塞·謝爾曼一八四一年五月以少尉身份護送科阿庫奇赴會，海軍中尉萊文·鮑威爾與約翰·麥克萊克林組織「蚊子船隊」，威廉·哈尼上校一八四〇年十二月率九十二人進入大沼澤地。塞米諾爾一方的核心是年輕戰士奧西奧拉，他以精準槍法聞名，一八三七年十月在白旗下談判時被捕，次年一月病逝於南卡羅來納的莫爾特里堡；老邁首領米卡諾皮於一八三七年三月代表多數首領簽署投降；「鱷魚」哈爾帕特·圖斯特努吉、科阿庫奇、薩姆·瓊斯、菲利普王、查卡伊卡、霍拉托·米科等人或死或俘；黑人塞米諾爾首領約翰·霍斯自莫爾頓堡脫逃後在大沼澤地重建據點；反對遷移的查利·埃馬斯拉則被奧西奧拉殺死，成為全面開戰的導火線之一。
peopleEn: The key federal figures were, before the shooting started, President Andrew Jackson and the Indian Office: Jackson's removal letter, together with the constant warnings from Lieutenant Colonel Duncan Clinch that the Seminoles had no intention of moving west, turned a local administrative quarrel into a military campaign. Florida Indian agent Wiley Thompson courted the chiefs, banned the sale of guns and powder, and stripped the office of chiefs who refused to move; he was killed in late October 1835 when his party was attacked. The command then rotated repeatedly: Edmund P. Gaines and Winfield Scott took the field first, Thomas Jesup took over in December 1836, Zachary Taylor assumed command in May 1838, and Walker Keith Armistead and then William Jenkins Worth followed in 1841. Major Francis L. Dade marched two companies out of Fort Brooke and was caught in an ambush, his son George Armistead among the dead. Ransom Clarke, one of the survivors, published his account of the fight in Florida in 1839, the only surviving narrative from the federal side, and Ethan Allen Hitchcock's journal carried the sharpest contemporary condemnation of the government for its broken treaty. William Tecumseh Sherman served as a lieutenant escorting Coacoochee to conference in May 1841; Navy lieutenants Levin Powell and John T. McLaughlin organized the 'Mosquito Fleet', and Colonel William S. Harney led ninety men into the Everglades in December 1840. On the Seminole side the central figure was the young warrior Osceola, renowned for his marksmanship, captured under a flag of truce in October 1837 and dead of disease within three months at Fort Moultrie in South Carolina. The aged chief Micanopy signed the capitulation of March 1837 on behalf of most of the chiefs; 'Alligator' Halpatter Tustenuggee, Coacoochee, Sam Jones, King Phillip, Chakaika and Holato Micco were killed, captured or driven into the Everglades; the Black Seminole leader John Horse escaped from Fort Marion and rebuilt a base deep in the Everglades; and Charley Emathla, who had opposed the war, was killed by Osceola on the trail to Fort King, one of the sparks that set the whole conflict alight.
kits: 卡面這件長槍，是西班牙大方陣的長柄矛（長槍 pica 與半長槍 media pica），十七世紀起便是步兵骨幹：長槍列在前排抵擋騎兵衝鋒，後方火槍隊才得以上膛射擊，密西西比河一役之後火槍與長槍再未分開。但到一八三五年，長槍早已退出野戰序列，只餘兩種用途：一是各州民兵操典仍列長槍科目，儀仗與校閱時才取出來；二是美國海軍陸戰隊的儀仗長槍，一八二五年由華盛頓居民贈予的那一支，如今仍懸於國會大廈。因此這場戰爭裡沒有任何一件長槍真正上陣，它標記的只是槍炮陣列時代的餘燼，與卡面「密西西比之後長矛和火槍一起站住」那句話正相隔一百七十年。真正決定勝負的是火器與彈藥。聯邦步兵用燧發滑膛火槍，一八一六年式 .58 口徑步槍與一八三五年定裝的新式步槍是主要型號，龍騎兵配手槍，砲兵帶六磅與十二磅滑膛野戰砲及小口徑榴彈砲，還把海軍艦砲架在駁船上溯河支援；志願兵多自備獵槍與冷兵器。塞米諾爾一方在湯普森禁售火槍之後，仍透過黑市與北方商人取得前裝步槍與獵槍，另備弓矢、戰斧、匕首、長矛與戰棍；弓矢在棕櫚叢中無聲而快，長矛的刺穿力在濘地與密林裡難以施展——這正是長矛在十八、十九世紀叢林戰爭中退場的原因。後勤同樣是裝備的一部分：獨木舟是深入沼澤的命脈，軍方購價每艘十至十五美元，海軍卻平均用到二百二十六美元；蒸汽船與帆船把糧食、彈藥運上威托拉庫奇河；一八三八至一八三九年間修出八百四十八英里車道，堡壘與巡邏隊才連成網。一八三八年泰勒試用獵犬追蹤失敗，一八四〇年佛羅里達從古巴買犬並僱用古巴嚮導，仍因犬隻無法越水追蹤而收效有限。
kitsEn: The pike on the card face is the Spanish infantry pike, the long pica and the media pica, which from the seventeenth century formed the backbone of the tercio: the pike line absorbed the charge of cavalry so that the musketeers behind it could load and fire, and after the Mississippi the pike and the musket were never again separated. But by 1835 the pike had long since left the field of battle and survived in only two guises: the drill regulations of the state militias still listed pike exercises, and the pike was taken out for inspection and ceremony only; and the Marine Corps' ceremonial pike, the one presented by the citizens of Washington in 1825, which still hangs in the Capitol. Not one pike was ever carried in a single action of this war. What the card records is only the afterglow of the pike-and-shot age, a hundred and seventy years removed from the line about the Mississippi. What actually decided engagements was firearms and ammunition. Federal infantry carried flintlock smoothbore muskets, the .58 caliber Model 1816 and the new model standardized in 1835 being the principal types; dragoons carried pistols; the artillery brought six- and twelve-pound smoothbore field pieces and light howitzers, and gunners mounted naval cannon on barges for river support; volunteers supplied their own hunting rifles and edged weapons. The Seminoles, though Thompson had banned the sale of guns and powder, still obtained muzzleloaders and hunting rifles through the black market and northern traders, and they also carried bows and arrows, tomahawks, knives, lances and war clubs. Arrows flew silently and fast through the palmetto, and a lance was useless in mud and close brush, which is precisely why the pike faded out of the wars of the woods in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. Logistics was part of the equipment as well. The dugout canoe was the lifeline of the swamp: the Army bought them at ten to fifteen dollars each, while the Navy averaged two hundred and twenty-six dollars. Steamers and sailing vessels carried grain and powder up the Withlacoochee, and eight hundred and forty-eight miles of wagon road were cut between 1838 and 1839 before the posts and patrols could be linked into a net. Bloodhounds were tried in 1838 at Taylor's request and failed; Florida bought dogs from Cuba in 1840 with Cuban handlers, and the War Department had to order them muzzled and leashed, and they could not follow a scent across water.
tactics: 聯邦的戰術在七年裡換了三次。第一階段是大縱隊決戰：一八三六年三月斯科特企圖以三路縱隊、合計五千人會合威托拉庫奇河灣，海軍配合從水路斷其退路，結果因道路未測、渡口未尋、糧秣耗盡而全盤落空；斯科特其後下令燒毀村莊與農作物，施行焦土政策，企圖以毀滅生計逼塞米諾爾出面。第二階段是封鎖與清剿。一八三八年起泰勒改以小堡壘連接車道封住佛羅里達北部，一八三九年春報告已建成五十三座新堡、開出八百四十八英里車道，巡邏隊以小分隊在堡與堡之間搜索；阿米斯蒂德與沃思接手後改在盛夏主動出擊，燒掉五百英畝塞米諾爾農田、趕走牲口，並以搜索與殲滅的名義派百人分隊連續掃蕩。海軍與緝私隊組成「蚊子船隊」，以縱帆快船、駁船與獨木舟巡河道，一八四〇年十二月至一八四一年一月，麥克萊克林率隊以獨木舟自東向西橫越大沼澤地，成為首批完成穿越的白人隊伍。塞米諾爾的回應是不打正面陣。伏擊、夜襲、襲擾堡壘，福特德雷恩、福特阿拉巴馬、福特班威爾先後遇襲或撤守，圍困威托拉庫奇河上的木柵哨所達四十八日，一八三六年七月二十三日燒毀南弗羅里達燈塔，都是拖延與擾亂的手段。他們熟悉棕櫚叢、鋸齒草泥濘與水道，隊形是散兵線而非線列，射擊一次即退，傷亡佔優時立刻散入沼澤，有時甚至奪取聯邦砲車回擊追兵。撤退與遷徙同樣是戰術：糧食被毀、村莊被燒，就整村退向大柏樹沼澤與大沼澤地，把正面戰爭拖成長達數年的消耗。
tacticsEn: Federal method changed three times in seven years. The first phase was the set-piece column march: in March 1836 Scott planned three columns totalling five thousand men to converge on the Cove of the Withlacoochee while the Navy worked the waterways to cut the Seminole retreat, and the whole design collapsed because the roads were unsurveyed, the fords were not found and the rations ran out; Scott then ordered the villages and the crops burned, scorched earth intended to destroy the Seminole livelihood and force them into the open. The second phase was blockade and sweep. From 1838 Taylor switched to small blockhouses linked by wagon roads to seal northern Florida, reporting in the spring of 1839 that fifty-three new posts had been built and eight hundred and forty-eight miles of road cut, with patrol parties searching between post and post. Under Armistead and Worth the army went on the offensive in high summer, burning five hundred acres of Seminole crops, driving off livestock, and sending hundred-man columns out under a search-and-destroy rubric. The Navy and the revenue cutters formed the 'Mosquito Fleet', with schooners, barges and canoes working the creeks; between December 1840 and January 1841 McLaughlin's force crossed the Everglades east to west in dugout canoes, the first white parties ever to complete the passage. The Seminole answer was never to stand in line. Ambush, night raid and the harassment of the forts, Fort Drane, Fort Alabama and Fort Barnwell all being attacked or abandoned, the forty-eight-day siege of the blockhouse on the Withlacoochee, and the burning of the Cape Florida lighthouse on July 23, 1836, were all instruments of delay and disruption. They knew the palmetto hammocks, the sawgrass mud and the waterways; their formation was a skirmish line, not a battalion front, they fired once and broke off, and when casualties mounted they dissolved into the swamp, sometimes turning captured artillery caissons against their pursuers. Retreat and migration were tactics in their own right: when stores were burned and villages were taken, whole communities withdrew toward the Big Cypress Swamp and the Everglades, stretching the war into a war of attrition lasting years.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下，但雙方記帳方式不同，數字多有出入。一八三五年十二月，戴德少校率一百一十人（兩個步兵連）離開福特布魯克，五日後在威托拉庫奇河上游遭伏擊，美方記錄僅三人生還，其中一人翌日被追殺，另有兩人於事後被俘；同一日奧西奧拉在福特金堡外擊殺湯普森等人。塞米諾爾開戰時約有九百至一千四百名戰士，總人口估計六千至一萬人；一八三六年傑薩普麾下兵力超過九千人，其中約半數為民兵與志願兵。一八三七年聖誕日奧基喬比湖之戰，泰勒以八百人對不足四百名塞米諾爾戰士：密蘇里民兵先敗，第六師二百人傷亡近四成，第四師一百六十人才把對方逐出，官方說只斃敵十餘人。物資與金錢方面，開戰時國會撥款六十二萬美元，一八三六年撥一百五十萬，一八三七年再撥一百六十萬，另撥五千美元用作談判；沃思時代每月耗費九萬三千三百美元（不含常備軍薪餉），而阿米斯蒂德用五萬五千美元收買首領，開價每名首領五千美元、次級首領二百美元、每名戰士三十美元加一支步槍。人員方面，陸軍、海軍與陸戰隊在佛州服役的正規兵共一萬零一百六十九人，另有約三萬民兵與志願兵；聯邦官方記錄死亡一千四百六十六人，多數死於疾病，陣亡數有三百二十八（馬洪）與二百六十九（米薩爾）兩說，海軍另有六十九或四十一之說，志願兵陣亡約五十五人。塞米諾爾方面的損失沒有任何一方作完整統計，諸說並存，只能說無從查考。全戰耗費估計三千萬至四千萬美元（馬洪），海軍開支約五十一萬一千美元。戰果上，至一八四一年春已送走四百五十人，另有二百三十六人候船；至一八四三年底共三千八百二十四名印第安人（含八百名黑人塞米諾爾）被運往印第安準州；沃思一八四三年十一月報告佛州只餘四十二名塞米諾爾戰士、三十三名米卡蘇基、十名克里克與十名塔拉哈西人，連婦孺合計約三百人。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked are roughly these, though the two sides tallied things differently and the numbers diverge. In December 1835 Major Dade marched out of Fort Brooke with one hundred and ten men in two companies; five days later his column was ambushed on the Withlacoochee above the river, the federal record showing only three survivors, one of whom was hunted down and killed the next day, while two others were taken prisoner afterwards, and on the same day Osceola shot Thompson and others outside Fort King. The Seminoles entered the war with between nine hundred and fourteen hundred warriors out of an estimated total population of six to ten thousand. Under Jesup in 1836 the federal force exceeded nine thousand men, about half of them militia and volunteers. At the Battle of Lake Okeechobee on Christmas Day 1837, Taylor had eight hundred men against fewer than four hundred Seminole warriors: the Missouri volunteers were broken first, the 6th Infantry lost nearly forty percent of its two hundred men, and only the 4th Infantry, a hundred and sixty strong, drove the Seminoles out of the hammock, with, by the official count, a dozen enemy dead. On money and materiel, Congress appropriated six hundred and twenty thousand dollars at the outbreak, one and a half million in 1836, another one and a half million in 1837, and five thousand for negotiation; under Worth the war cost ninety-three thousand three hundred dollars a month on top of regular pay, while Armistead had fifty-five thousand dollars for buying chiefs, offering five thousand dollars a head to each chief, two hundred to lesser chiefs, and thirty dollars plus a musket to every warrior. On personnel: ten thousand one hundred and sixty-nine regulars of the Army, Navy and Marine Corps served in Florida, joined by roughly thirty thousand militiamen and volunteers; federal records show one thousand four hundred and sixty-six deaths, mostly from disease, with battle deaths given as three hundred and twenty-eight in one standard history and two hundred and sixty-nine in another, navy dead as sixty-nine or forty-one, and volunteer dead as about fifty-five. The Seminole side was never counted by anyone, and the histories can only say that no record survives and the accounts differ. Total cost is estimated at thirty to forty million dollars, with naval expenditure of about five hundred and eleven thousand. On results: four hundred and fifty were shipped west by the spring of 1841, with two hundred and thirty-six more waiting for transport; by the end of 1843 a total of three thousand eight hundred and twenty-four Indians, including eight hundred Black Seminoles, had been moved to Indian Territory west of the Mississippi; in November 1843 Worth reported only forty-two Seminole warriors, thirty-three Mikasukis, ten Creeks and ten Tallahassees left in Florida, about three hundred people including women and children.
cause: 開戰的起因是美國聯邦要把塞米諾爾人遷出佛羅里達。一八三〇年的《印第安人遷移法》給了政策框架，一八三二年春天在奧克萊瓦哈河畔佩恩登陸處談判時，七名首領被要求代表全體簽署遷往密西西比河西岸克里克保留地的條約；一八三三年聯邦政府逕行用印，一八三四年參議院批准，給三年遷移期限，聯邦政府按一八三二年起算，期望一八三五年就緒。返回佛羅里達的多數首領立刻聲明未曾簽署、或是被脅迫，連部分聯邦軍官都認為條約措辭有詐。移民與土地帶來的壓力、拓殖者的湧入，以及聯邦對黑奴逃跑與潛入佛州勢力的憂慮，令遷移成為執行的政策而非可談的選項。一八三四年出任印第安事務官的威利·湯普森不斷遊說，同時禁止售賣火槍與火藥，收繳不肯遷移者的首領權位；一八三五年三月傑克遜致信塞米諾爾首領，明言若拒絕遷移即以武力把他們遷走。首領要求三十日回覆，一個月後明確拒絕；八月郵差達爾頓在送信途中被殺；十一月查利·埃馬斯拉率族人前往福特布魯克登船西遷，被其他塞米諾爾視為背叛，奧西奧拉在通往福特金堡的路上將他殺死。一八三五年十月末，奧西奧拉的人在福特金堡外擊殺湯普森與數人，同一時期聯邦已決定派兵強制執行遷移，雙方的對撞就此不可收拾。導火索是政治性的：聯邦不能承認自己在條約上失信，而塞米諾爾寧可退入沼澤，也不肯離開祖先之地。
causeEn: The war began because the United States decided to move the Seminoles out of Florida. The Indian Removal Act of 1830 supplied the legal frame; in the spring of 1832, at Payne's Landing on the Oklawaha River, seven chiefs were required to sign for the whole people a treaty sending the Seminoles west of the Mississippi to the Creek reservation. The federal government drew up the instrument in 1833, the Senate ratified it in 1834, and it allowed three years to move, the government counting from 1832 and expecting everyone out in 1835. Most of the chiefs who came home immediately denied having signed, or said they had been forced to, and some federal officers themselves thought the treaty had been worded as a swindle. Pressure from settlers and land hunger, and federal anxiety over fugitive slaves and the Black Seminoles, turned removal from a negotiable item into an order to be executed. Wiley Thompson, appointed Indian agent in 1834, courted the chiefs endlessly while banning the sale of guns and powder and stripping the office of chiefs who would not go; in March 1835 Jackson wrote to the Seminole leaders that if they refused to move he had directed the commanding officer to remove them by force. The chiefs asked for thirty days to answer, and a month later refused outright. In August a mail carrier, Dalton, was killed on the road; in November Charley Emathla took his people to Fort Brooke to board ships for the west, which the other Seminoles read as betrayal, and Osceola killed him on the trail to Fort King. In late October 1835 Osceola's men shot Thompson and several others outside Fort King, and at the same moment the federal government had already resolved to enforce removal by troops. The collision was therefore political in origin: the United States could not afford to be seen to have broken its own treaty, and the Seminoles would rather retreat into the swamp than leave the land of their ancestors.
impact: 影響最深遠的一層是戰爭的代價與它留下的未解難題。這場衝突被後世視為美國歷時最長、耗費最巨的印第安戰爭：花費估計三千萬至四千萬美元，超過一場規模遠為龐大的美墨戰爭；聯邦投入一萬餘名正規軍與約三萬民兵志願兵，仍未能把佛州境內的塞米諾爾人清剿乾淨。佛羅里達建州因此一延再延，直到一八四五年才獲准入聯邦。一八四二年八月國會通過《武裝拓殖法》，撥地給願意防衛自己的移民，一八四二至一八四三年間登記者一千三百一十七宗、共二十一萬零七百二十英畝，此法日後成為一八六二年《宅地法》的先聲。制度與倫理上的裂痕同樣深：將奧西奧拉、科阿庫奇等首領在白旗下談判時羈押，雖在戰術上省了許多兵力，卻被同時代視為背信，之後所有談判都難以再取信任；獵犬追蹤的做法在佛州引發輿論反對，國防部被迫要求犬隻戴口套繫繩；哈尼上校一八四〇年在大沼澤地懸吊俘虜並率隊襲營的做法，經地方議會表彰後反而掩蓋了作戰方式的爭議。聯邦把這場戰爭的開支與軍隊擴張視為西進的前奏，卻也在國內養成了對長期戰事、對民兵與常備軍權限的爭論；被運往西部的三千餘名塞米諾爾人在克里克保留地與新同伴摩擦不斷，遷徙後的生計問題並未解決。一八四二年的所謂結束並未帶來和解，一八五五至一八五八年的第三次塞米諾爾戰爭隨即爆發，佛羅里達的印第安問題延續至今。對卡上這件器物而言，這場戰爭也是長槍退場的註腳：在沼澤、棕櫚叢與鋸齒草泥濘之中，三百年的長槍陣列毫無用處，最終被收進操典與儀仗的櫥櫃裡，成為歷史的殘像。
impactEn: The deepest consequences were the cost of the war and the unresolved problem it left behind. Later generations counted it as the longest and most expensive Indian war the United States fought: an estimated thirty to forty million dollars, more than a war of far greater size, the Mexican war, and a commitment of more than ten thousand regulars and some thirty thousand volunteers, and still the Seminoles of Florida were not cleared out. Florida's admission as a state was postponed again and again until 1845. In August 1842 Congress passed the Armed Occupation Act, granting land to settlers willing to defend themselves, and between 1842 and 1843 one thousand three hundred and seventeen claims were registered covering two hundred and ten thousand seven hundred and twenty acres, a measure that would later foreshadow the Homestead Act of 1862. The institutional and ethical fractures ran just as deep. Seizing Osceola, Coacoochee and other chiefs while they talked under a flag of truce saved the army a great deal of fighting, but was read at the time as bad faith, and every negotiation after it was harder to trust; the use of bloodhounds in Florida drew public protest, and the War Department had to order the dogs muzzled and leashed; and Colonel Harney's hanging of prisoners and his attacks on camp in the Everglades in December 1840 were publicly commended by the territorial council, which buried the argument about how the war was being fought. The federal government treated the expenditure and the expanded army as a rehearsal for expansion to the west, but the war also produced a domestic argument about the cost of long campaigns and about the limits of militia and regular authority. The more than three thousand Seminoles shipped west did not fare well either, rubbing shoulders with their new Creek neighbours on the reservation; the problems of removal were not solved by removal. The so-called ending of 1842 brought no reconciliation: the Third Seminole War broke out in 1855 and ran to 1858, and the Florida Indian question was never closed. For the object on this card, the war is also a footnote to the retirement of the pike: in swamp, palmetto and sawgrass mud, three centuries of pike formation were of no use at all, and the pike was finally shut in the drill manual and the ceremonial cupboard as a relic of history.
result: 結果是一場沒有和平條約的『結束』。一八四二年，沃思准許殘餘塞米諾爾人留在佛州西南部與大沼澤地的非正式保留地，作為交換，他獲授權在自選日期宣告戰事結束；一八四二年八月十四日他宣布第二次塞米諾爾戰爭結束，時在佛州的美軍尚有第一、二、三師等部共一千八百九十人。戰爭從未簽訂和約，最後一次有組織的戰鬥發生在一八四二年：北佛羅里達『虎尾』蒂格爾·塔斯特努吉一夥襲擾拓殖者，威廉·貝利率五十二人民兵追擊三日，在沼澤營地將二十四人全部擊殺，十六歲的威廉·韋斯利·漢金斯擊中最後一槍。十一月沃思返回佛州後，認為北部首領久拖不決，遂下令將『虎尾』與奧蒂亞奇一併押解西遷，『虎尾』病重，死於紐奧良候船之時。清點結果顯示，塞米諾爾人從未被徹底消滅：一八四三年十一月沃思報告佛州僅餘四十二名塞米諾爾戰士、三十三名米卡蘇基、十名克里克與十名塔拉哈西人，連婦孺約三百人；此後仍不斷有零星襲擊，直到聯邦承認他們在西南佛州的居住權。到一八四三年底，三千八百二十四名印第安人（含八百名黑人塞米諾爾）被運往密西西比河西岸的印第安準州，其後的登記人數與死亡，都令『遷移完成』成為一句不確定的話。軍事上聯邦取得了大部分勝利，卻沒能追蹤到沼澤深處，最終以宣布結束代替取勝；卡面上的長槍也在同一段時間裡退出了軍隊序列，只在民兵操典與海軍陸戰隊的儀仗中留到最後。
resultEn: The outcome was an ending with no peace treaty behind it. In 1842 Worth obtained authorization to leave the remaining Seminoles on an informal reservation in southwestern Florida and the Everglades, and in exchange he was permitted to declare the war over on a date of his choosing; on August 14, 1842 he declared the Second Seminole War ended, with the federal force in Florida still numbering about one thousand eight hundred and ninety men from the 1st, 2nd and 3rd Infantry and other units. No peace treaty was ever signed, and the last organized action of the war came in 1842, when a band under 'Tiger Tail' in northern Florida harried the settlers and a fifty-two-man posse under William Bailey pursued them for three days, surprising their camp in the swamp and killing all twenty-four of them; the sixteen-year-old William Wesley Hankins fired the last shot of the Second Seminole War. Worth returned to Florida in November 1842, judged that the northern chiefs had procrastinated too long, and ordered 'Tiger Tail' and Otiarche taken and sent west; 'Tiger Tail' was so ill he had to be carried on a litter and died in New Orleans while waiting for transport. The count shows the Seminoles were never extinguished. In November 1843 Worth reported only forty-two Seminole warriors, thirty-three Mikasukis, ten Creeks and ten Tallahassees in Florida, about three hundred people with women and children; scattered attacks continued for years, and the federal government eventually recognized the right of the survivors to live in southwestern Florida. By the end of 1843 three thousand eight hundred and twenty-four Indians, including eight hundred Black Seminoles, had been shipped to Indian Territory west of the Mississippi, and the registers and the deaths that followed made removal complete an uncertain claim. Militarily the United States won most of what it set out to win, but it could not follow the Seminoles into the depth of the swamp and substituted a declaration of closure for a victory. In the same years the pike on the card face left the order of battle for good, surviving only in the militia drill manuals and in the ceremonial hands of the Marine Corps.
